flagged.sentence: 一种解释是：他没有把出海说成上策，只说成不得已。

A remote station of a few people, supplies good for another stretch of time, communications down, the next resupply date unknown: does everyone stay and endure, or does someone go out and risk seeking help?
只说“你看着办”却不讲失败的下场，责任就悬在半空。
作者说，南乔治亚航程的记述依据逐日写下的简略笔记，笔记通常只记距离、船位和天气，航程中的具体经过则来自记忆。

S-SOUTH.title: Ernest Shackleton, South (1920 printing), archive.org OCR

episode.outcome: The James Caird runs into a small cove in King Haakon Bay and all six get safely ashore and drink fresh water. Landing is not the end of the search for help: the boat is weakened and Stromness is still 150 miles away by sea, so the account turns to crossing the island. The rudder lost at the landing later drifts back into the cove. On May 15 they sail to the head of the bay and land among hundreds of sea-elephants, which ends their food worries.
episode.quote: in a few minutes we were all safe on the beach, with the boat floating in the surging water just off the shore. We heard a gurgling sound that was sweet music in our ears, and, peering around, found a stream of fresh water almost at our feet.

episode.outcome: In the preface, the twenty-two men left on Elephant Island hold out for four and a half months. After several relief attempts, the Chilean Government's Yelcho, under Luis Pardo, completes the last and successful rescue.
episode.quote: Finally, it was the Chilian Government that was directly responsible for the rescue of my comrades.

additions.why: The rudder lost on landing night drifted back into the cove on May 13 and was recovered. The draft stops at 'a serious loss' and never mentions the recovery, so readers will think the boat had no rudder from then on.

additions.start: We rounded a high, glacier-worn bluff
additions.end: our anxieties with regard to food disappeared.
additions.why: The draft ends with 'they still had to sail to the head of the bay'. The reading range already has the result: on May 15 they reached the head of the bay and found plenty of sea-elephants, which ended the food shortage. This is the immediate next turn after the landing.

claims.sentence: 作者说，南乔治亚航程的记述依据逐日写下的简略笔记，笔记通常只记距离、船位和天气，航程中的具体经过则来自记忆。
claims.scope: Chapter IX, the source-description paragraph at p.165. The original says 'usually' and the draft keeps 'usually', so the scope is accurate.

quote.quote: This record of the voyage to South Georgia is based upon Scanty notes made day by day. The notes dealt usually with the bare facts of distances, positions, and weather, but our memories retained the incidents of the passing days

claims.sentence: 本文未对照其他当事人的记录核实
claims.scope: Describes what this piece actually checked: only one book, South, was consulted. It says nothing about whether anyone else verified the account at the time, so it should not be read as 'no independent check exists'.

quote.quote: This record of the voyage to South Georgia is based upon Scanty notes made day by day.

claims.fix: Keep the wording limited to 'this piece has not cross-checked', and do not extend it to 'no third party has ever verified'.

claims.sentence: 文森特为什么垮掉，队长自己说难以解释，本文不替他补心理。
claims.scope: Chapter IX, the night after the great wave (around p.175). No other explanation appears in the reading range.

quote.quote: Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and I could not easily account for his collapse.

claims.sentence: 文森特在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉
claims.scope: Same passage in Chapter IX as N2.

quote.quote: I could not easily account for his collapse

context_issues.problem: The draft presents the lost rudder as a final outcome ('在海滩和够得着的岩石间仔细搜寻也没找到，这是严重的损失'). In the reading range the rudder drifted back into the cove on May 13 and was recovered. As written, the passage misleads readers.

quote.quote: The rudder, with all the broad Atlantic to sail in and the coasts of two continents to search for a resting-place, came bobbing back into our cove.

context_issues.problem: The draft ends with 'they still had to sail to the head of the bay'. The reading range shows they reached it on May 15 and found plenty of sea-elephants, so the food problem was solved. Add a sentence, or explicitly say the account continues from there to the island crossing.

quote.quote: There were hundreds of sea-elephants lying about, and our anxieties with regard to food disappeared.

review.overall: The draft covers the voyage's outcome and the rescue of the Elephant Island party fairly completely. One fix is required: the rudder was lost but recovered, and the draft wrongly leaves it as a lost-for-good outcome. The negative and limitation statements are accurately scoped.
